"Right. Go on, then."

"I'm sorry — I'm achy and wrung out, barely keeping food down. I need help. Please."
"Rest and clean water aren't cutting it. If this turns, I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. I need someone who knows what they're doing."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Ivan owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.

"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."

"Never mind the sickness I'm fighting — we got it handled. Thanks anyway."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Ivan always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"Okay. That's — I need a minute. A long minute."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."

"Take your time."
"This one — Açaí. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"This one — Cush-cush Yam. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."

"I should go. You know where to find me."

"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can we talk?" Quinn sits down near you. "Just... talk. Like people used to."
They light up a little when they see you.
Something crosses their face — quick, then gone. The practiced expression clicks back into place.
"Okay." Quinn looks down. "Okay, you got me. I wasn't a doctor. I was a bartender. The truth felt small. The lie felt like someone worth keeping around." Their voice is small.
"You're really going to make me say it again?" Quinn rubs their face. "Fine — but it's the same truth as last time."
"The cistern's nearly dry — 2 liters left. I need someone to haul water with me at first light. Two of us, half the trips. Will you come?"
"2 liters. That's today's drinking water, and then we're boiling creek water and hoping. We walk together and each carry two liters back. Creek water still needs boiling."
Move next to your partner, on the same side of the Haven door.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Since Scott died... I keep expecting to see Scott at the fire. Stupid."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.

"Yeah? What's up?"
They answer at length. They nod back, slowly.
They answer at length. A grin breaks through, quick and warm.
They answer at length. You point at yourself, then at them, then at the fire. Together. They get it.
A gesture, patient and clear: palms up, then toward you.
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"This was good." They mean it.
"We gave them a good burial. Doesn't feel like enough, does it?"
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
You walk to the trap line with Onni. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"Thanks. ...Thanks for saying that."
"We lost Nattawut, Quinn and Wanjiru this week. I keep setting out extra portions. Stupid."
"Out there? With YOU leading? ...Let me think about it."
You show them Jewelweed — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Let me sit with all that. We'll pick it up later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Have you — sorry. I keep thinking about them. ...sorry."
Ava has an edge today — something curdled.
"Most days I don't think about it. Today I am. Appreciate you noticing."
"Nattawut is gone, Quinn is gone, and Wanjiru is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"I keep turning over the last thing Wanjiru said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"The fire feels smaller without Wanjiru. The rest of us will have to be bigger."
"Still on what's been happening. It'll pass."
You show them Jewelweed — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Go on, then. I'll be thinking good thoughts at you."

"This was good." They mean it.

lastSay: d88: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Ava Garcia is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d88: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d88: 🕯️ Ava Garcia is dead — the wild. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d88: What Ava kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d88: No one is left to pick up the Codex. The village dies out — quietly, the way villages do. The season ends here.
